notes:
Summary: Account has stalled and effectively closed-won to competitor for immediate rollout. Primary friction: integration gaps (SDK streaming hooks & observability/tracing), and SAML issues that conflict with their IdP. Procurement froze spend in Jan 2026 after headcount reduction; internal champion (Sr. ML Eng) left in mid-Jan.

Key quotes / call snippets:
- "We like Redwood's latency but we can't ship without full tracing + span IDs in-band to our APM yet." (Director, ML)
- "If the SDK can't stream with our browser client and we can't tie traces back, it's a blocker for security and SRE signoff."

Timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-09-10: Lead created via webinar signup (ML infra leads).
- 2025-10-02: Intro call (Evan P.). high-level requirements captured: VPC, SSO, tracing, 50–100 qps baseline.
- 2025-11-18: Demo of hosted API; requested dedicated performance numbers.
- 2025-12-01: POC kickoff (small dedicated pool); engineering asked for JS SDK streaming + trace headers support.
- 2025-12-10: SE (Maya) delivered sample patch for trace header propagation; engineering requested deeper tracing hooks (span IDs and per-token traces).
- 2026-01-08: Procurement pause announced (company-wide hiring & cost freeze).
- 2026-01-19: Primary champion left role; champion introduced internal replacement but low bandwidth.
- 2026-02-15: Final demo vs competitor (CloudPrompt) — competitor showed built-in SSO flow and APM integration; customer indicated preference.
- 2026-02-28: Last active touchpoint; customer unresponsive after follow-ups.

Technical notes / integration friction detail:
- SDK gaps: No official browser-optimized JS SDK with streaming + reconnect semantics that meets Pinegrove's client architecture. They attempted to use an unofficial wrapper; edge cases caused token duplication and provenance issues.
- Auth: SAML assertion mapping requires attribute-level mapping that Redwood's current SAML connector doesn't expose (requested by Pinegrove SSO team).
- Observability: Pinegrove requires per-request span IDs pushed as part of token metadata so their APM (Dataduct) can stitch llm calls into traces. Current workaround (X-Request-Id header) insufficient.
- Tracing hooks: They wanted SDK APIs to emit spans locally before sending tokens so their SRE can measure per-token latency. Redwood SE provided a shim but customer wanted an official SDK-level contract and guarantee.

Actions taken by Redwood:
- SE created a technical gap doc and sample shim (RED-INF-4123).
- Security runbook and SAML mapping doc shared (/drive/security/pinegrove_security_faq.md).
- Proposal for trimmed POC (no-trace mode) and staging-only dedicated pool offered to reduce scope and cost.
- Pricing concession proposed (15% off year 1) to offset hiring freeze.

Current status: Account is effectively stalled / closed-lost for near-term rollout. Customer evaluating CloudPrompt for faster SSO + APM integration. Procurement freeze and lack of champion means low chance to close before 2026-06 unless exec intervention.

Recommended next steps (CRM):
- Mark as stalled; set re-engage cadence for 2026-05.
- Offer a small co-build/engineering engagement to deliver official JS streaming SDK + tracing hooks (timeboxed 6 weeks) — require EPD approval.
- Track competitor feature parity (CloudPrompt SSO connector + Dataduct integration).
- Keep SE notes on RED-INF tickets open; escalate to product for SDK roadmap consideration.

Short next-step for AE: "Hold until May; ask for CHRO/IT budget update and if champion re-hired; offer 6-week eng co-build if they can commit to a pilot budget"

CRM notes tone: choppy bullets, lots of quoted lines, repeated asks. See linked artifacts for details.
